message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI (Linux AArch64)
on:
  workflow_call:
jobs:
  build:
    name: Linux AArch64
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04-arm # Lowest version that support Vulkan 1.3.
    steps:
    - name: Check out repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - name: Install System Packages
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y libvulkan-dev
    - name: Update Rust
      run: rustup update stable
    - name: Install Rust nightly
      run: rustup toolchain install nightly
    - name: Install additional Rust components
      run: rustup component add rust-src --toolchain nightly
    - name: Install additional Rust targets
      run: rustup target add aarch64-unknown-none-softfloat
    - name: Cache cargo registry
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-
    - name: Install additional tools
      run: cargo install project
    - name: Lint Rust sources
      run: project lint
    - name: Build
      run: project build -r
    - name: Run tests
      run: cargo test
",
  "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly downloads Rust crate dependencies (via `cargo install project`, `project build`, and `cargo test`) on every run. Adding a cache for `~/.cargo/registry` and `~/.cargo/git` keyed by the repository's `Cargo.lock` avoids redundant downloads and extraction. This matches the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) which has experimental support showing 6–20% elapsed-time savings in similar dependency-caching scenarios (Go modules, Gradle, pip). The cache is safe because the lockfile pins transitive dependencies, and the runner environment (ubuntu-22.04-arm) is constant.",
  "evidence_ids": [
    "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9",
    "experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"
  ]
}
